 "Twisty" and "chaotic" 8-part drama with House of Guinness star is streaming now on Netflix 
 It is based on a real-life, high-profile scandal.
 By Rebecca Sayce Published: 19 November 2026 %0A%09<path d="M240,128a15.74,15.74,0,0,1-7.6,13.51L88.32,229.65a16,16,0,0,1-16.2.3A15.86,15.86,0,0,1,64,216.13V39.87a15.86,15.86,0,0,1,8.12-13.82,16,16,0,0,1,16.2.3L232.4,114.49A15.74,15.74,0,0,1,240,128Z">%0A</path></svg>" width="60" height="60" alt="Play video"/> A drama hailed as "mind-boggling" and "twisty" is streaming now on Netflix. Starring House of Guinness ' Anthony Boyle and Weapons ' Julia Garner , The Altruists follows the meteoric rise and eventual collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX. The company is run by Sam Bankman-Fried (Boyle), founder of FTX and Alameda Research, and Caroline Ellison (Garner), CEO of Alameda Research and Bankman-Fried’s girlfriend.
 Both were at the helm when FTX collapsed in November 2022, when it was found that Alameda had used FTX customer funds in violation of the FTX terms of service.
 Netflix described the eight-part series as "twisty", with a synopsis reading: "Young, idealistic and suddenly worth billions, they tried to do good - but unleashed the worst in each other. A toxic love story inspired by a real fraud."
 Netflix Related: Best streaming services UK 2026 – including Disney Plus, Netflix, iPlayer and Apple TV 
 The cast also includes Alex Lawther ( The End of the F***ing World ), Matt Rife ( Scrubs ), Madison Hu ( Rooster ), Hudson Williams ( Heated Rivalry) , Karan Soni ( Deadpool ), Eugene Young, and Naomi Okada.
 The Altruists has received mixed reviews from critics, with many praising Garner's performance. Others have criticised how the show depicted its source material.
 What to Read Next
 The Guardian called it "chaotic" and "mind-boggling", adding: "Anchored by brilliant performances from Boyle and Garner, two of the best young screen actors working today, and supported by fine turns elsewhere (especially from Karan Soni as the most emotionally brutalised of SBF’s victims), The Altruists stays just the right side of coherent."
 Radio Times wrote: "While Boyle makes a solid attempt at capturing Sam, his performance is occasionally cartoonish. It’s Garner who is the series’ standout. She has form playing high-profile liars, having portrayed fake heiress Anna Delvey in Netflix’s Inventing Anna . 
 "She captures Caroline’s complex emotional state, which sees her eventually turn on her former lover and business partner to become the prosecution’s star witness. Garner does it with a chameleon-like ease that makes her work so fun and watchable."
 Netflix Related: Hugh Bonneville's "superb" drama hailed as "a twisty, gripping story" is coming to Netflix 
 Time , however, thought the series was "muddled" and "boring", arguing: " The Altruists stumbles because, even as its exaggeration of the Sam-and-Caroline stuff distorts the most basic elements of the true story, it also strains to depict in detail what really happened at FTX."
 The Hollywood Reporter called The Altruists "intriguing but unsatisfying", while Variety thought it "failed to get a handle" on its narrative.
 The Altruists is streaming now on Netflix.
